analysis:
Examined ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift head 552-1694 and the ProviderLoop+PlannedDisconnect.swift patch.

ModelLoading: the only change is head 1191. A non-shutdown unload now skips persistLoadedModelSet when servingDrain.owner == .addonHold. This affects only the local startup-preload plan; it is an availability/persistence choice. It does not touch weight-hash verification at 559-662 (T-012, T-027), SSD cache eligibility or cacheEligibleWeightHash (T-041), or admission. No security regression was identified.

PlannedDisconnect, waitForSafeDisconnect (head 9-15): a new underAddonHold flag is added. fenceAllowed refuses the barrier during an add-on hold unless the caller is the planned reconnect, and it is rechecked after the drain wait.

PlannedDisconnect, ownsPlannedReconnect (head 38-40): the reconnect loop may now run under an .addonHold owner. The comment says the hold keeps ownership, so a fresh registration cannot reopen admission. However, finishPlannedReconnect (head ~97-100) still runs localResponseTracker.setAccepting(!servingDrain.refusing) and then calls reassertAddonHoldAfterReconnect, whose implementation was not supplied.

PlannedDisconnect, resumeAfterAddonHold (head 116-129): it releases the hold. If a retirement reconnect is pending, it then re-begins a .reconnect drain; if a disconnect barrier is pending, it requests a planned reconnect.

Relevant boundaries are TB-002 and TB-011/T-053, covering connection replacement and registration and whether work is admitted on a fenced connection. The possible concern is a window in which admission could reopen between registration and the reassert. The added comments assert this cannot happen, but servingDrain.refusing semantics for the addonHold owner and resumeAddonHold were not visible. These are availability/admission contracts, not evidence of plaintext exposure.

Questions for integration:
- Does servingDrain.refusing stay true under .addonHold?
- Does reassertAddonHoldAfterReconnect preserve refusal?
- Does resumeAfterAddonHold avoid accepting work on a connection fenced by a barrier before re-registration?

No findings.
